clue.text: First mate sporting new uniform

parts.note: Eve was the first woman, mate of Adam

explanation.surface: A ship's first officer turns out in a fresh uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First mate' looks nautical but means Adam's partner; 'sporting' is just a link: she is wearing the N.
explanation.definitionFit: Uniform as an adjective means level and consistent throughout, a synonym.

clue.text: Scales a for, with their help

definitions.text: Scales a for, with their help

parts.words: Scales a for, with their help
parts.note: read as moving stairs that let you climb a rocky hill without effort; the printed 'for' is an OCR slip for 'tor', a rocky peak

explanation.surface: A climber gets up a rocky peak with some mechanical assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: A tor is a rocky hill on English moorland. Moving stairs let you go up one without climbing; the letters of SCALES A TOR also rearrange into the answer, an unflagged bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving staircases carry people upward, so they help anyone scale a height.

clue.text: Bush-dweller blending into the landscape

indicators.note: the animal's name merges into the run of letters across the words that follow, so it sits inside them

explanation.surface: A wild animal is camouflaged against the scenery.
explanation.definitionFit: This African antelope lives in the bush, so it is a dweller there.

clue.text: Gloomy disposition?

parts.note: read not as a melancholy temperament but as a dark place where the dead are disposed of, or criminals operate

explanation.surface: Someone is described as having a melancholy temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disposition' pretends to mean temperament; it is the act of disposing, and the gloomy place is the realm of the dead in myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades, the realm of departed souls, is a dark gloomy place where the dead are put.

clue.text: Middleman right to get a profit after upsetting falls

indicators.note: in a down clue, upsetting turns the whole string upside down so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: the middle letter of the word man
a gain is a profit

explanation.surface: A go-between makes money after someone's downfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Middleman' looks like a broker but is the middle of 'man'. 'upsetting' turns ARAGAIN round as a whole.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous waterfalls on the US-Canada border bear this name.

clue.text: Retire maybe, to a place in Africa

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word retire could be some other arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: Someone thinks of settling in Africa when they stop working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges RETIRE into ERITRE, then A is added.
explanation.definitionFit: This country lies on the Red Sea coast of the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Seep right out of sewer-pipes'—- brushes all that's left

indicators.note: these letters are to be removed from the word that follows, leaving what remains

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Leaking drains are cleaned up with a scrub of whatever remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' strips S, E, E, P and R from SEWERPIPES, leaving W, I, P, E, S; 'all that's left' tells you to take the remainder. The odd punctuation is the OCR's.
explanation.definitionFit: To brush something is to wipe or sweep it lightly, a synonym.

clue.text: River teal flying off — the plan is to bring them back

definitions.text: the plan is to bring them back
definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for the noun: the act of bringing back

indicators.note: the birds scattering in flight signals that the letters of the two words are scattered too

explanation.surface: Ducks have flown from the river and someone wants them returned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying off' rearranges RIVER TEAL; the definition is a loose phrase for getting something back.
explanation.definitionFit: Recovering something lost is exactly the act of getting it back, so this describes recovery.

clue.text: The way five hundred initially discovered sea transport

indicators.note: says the numeral letter is placed at the start, before the other piece

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for five hundred
how means the way something is done

explanation.surface: Explorers early on worked out how to cross the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: An Arab sailing vessel with a lateen sail, a kind of boat.

clue.text: A hold-up in main line if betel nuts to be provided

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so the letters of the two words that follow go wild

explanation.surface: Betel nuts are supplied in case of a delay on the main railway line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' makes IFEBELT. 'Main' is the old word for the open sea; 'hold-up' means something that keeps you afloat, not a delay.
explanation.definitionFit: A buoyant ring keeps a person up when they are in the sea, the main.

clue.text: Mock serenade in which vicar has hair tousled

indicators.note: tousled hair is messed up, so the letters of vicar and hair are jumbled

explanation.surface: A clergyman with ruffled hair is the victim of a mocking song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tousled' mixes VICAR and HAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy mock serenade of banging pans, made to newlyweds or unpopular people, is this rowdy custom.

clue.text: Small boy placed books back to front

parts.note: to have placed something is to have put it

indicators.note: the books abbreviation is turned round so its letters run the other way

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A child shelved the books the wrong way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A cherubic little boy figure in Renaissance art, a winged child.

clue.text: Get stuck in the building

definitions.meaning: to become fixed or wedged somewhere
a small house, such as a gatekeeper's or hunting cabin

explanation.definitionFit: A bone can become wedged in the throat; a gatekeeper's cottage or Masonic hall is one too.

clue.text: A cryptic reminder of Sunday Times initial clue?

definitions.text: A cryptic reminder of Sunday Times initial clue?

parts.words: A cryptic reminder of Sunday Times initial clue?
parts.note: the clue describes itself: read the opening letter of each of its eight words in order

explanation.surface: Something hints at the first clue in the newspaper's puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of A Cryptic Reminder Of Sunday Times Initial Clue spell the answer, which is itself a puzzle in which initials spell a word; the first clue of the puzzle is also an across one.
explanation.definitionFit: A composition where the first letters of lines or words spell out a word is this kind of puzzle.

clue.text: Two girls making the organ stop

parts.note: Clara is a girl's name
Bella is another girl's name

explanation.surface: Two young women bring the organ to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stop' looks like a verb about halting the organ; it is the noun, a set of pipes.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the name of a flute-like set of pipes on an organ, one of its registers.

clue.text: As three go off, she appears

indicators.note: go off means to explode, so the letters of as and three are blown apart

explanation.surface: When a trio leaves, a woman shows up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go off' rearranges AS THREE into a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's first name, so she is an example of a female person.

clue.text: Broken rod I found in remains of fire became ornament

indicators.note: the jumbled letters sit inside the word for the remains of a fire

parts.note: an ember is a glowing piece left after a fire

indicators.note: broken signals that the letters of rod and I come apart and reassemble

explanation.surface: A snapped rod discovered in the ashes was turned into a decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' makes ROID and 'found in' places it within the remains; 'became' is a link, and the definition is a verb, to decorate.
explanation.definitionFit: To decorate cloth with needlework, or to add flourishes to a story, is to adorn it.

clue.text: Gunners retreating on adversary's appearance

indicators.note: going backwards, so the letters of the gunners' abbreviation are read in reverse

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners of the British Army
an adversary is a rival; the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Soldiers fall back when the enemy turns up.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming onto the scene is turning up, so an arrival is a showing up.

clue.text: Artist clothed for bad weather

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the garment worn in it

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
dressed in a coat, so clothed

explanation.surface: A painter is dressed up against the rain.
explanation.definitionFit: A waterproof garment worn when it is wet outside.

clue.text: Nothing in crib to rock? It's inhuman!

indicators.note: the letter for nothing goes inside the jumbled letters
to rock is to shake, so the letters of crib and to are shaken up

parts.note: O, a zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Someone finds an empty cradle being rocked and calls it heartless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rock' makes ROBTIC, and 'in' sets the zero within it; the surface's empty cradle is a red herring.
explanation.definitionFit: Machine-like and mechanical, lacking human warmth.

clue.text: Colonels, we hear, are attached to this pipe?

definitions.text: Colonels, we hear, are attached to this pipe?

parts.words: Colonels, we hear, are attached to this pipe?
parts.note: officers sound like the seeds of maize, which grow on the cob that is made into a smoker's bowl

explanation.surface: Army officers are said to be fond of a certain pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Colonels' sounds like kernels, the grains that sit on a maize cob; a cob hollowed out makes a cheap tobacco pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: A tobacco pipe whose bowl is made from a dried maize ear.

clue.text: Flirt outrageously with royalty? He can't be serious!

indicators.note: behaving shockingly, so the letters of flirt are thrown about

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone flirts shamelessly with royals and is told off for not being serious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outrageously' rearranges FLIRT into TRIFL, then ER (the Queen) is added.
explanation.definitionFit: A frivolous person who treats things lightly is never earnest.

clue.text: Two youth leaders on edge, after catching fish

indicators.note: the two opening letters hold the fish between them
the leaders of two and youth are their opening letters

parts.note: the witch is a flatfish, also called witch flounder

explanation.surface: Two youngsters grow nervous after landing a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' takes T and Y, and 'catching' wraps them round WITCH; 'after' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Nervous and jumpy, as if about to twitch.

clue.text: Cold reaction perhaps when a bit's left out of these compositions?

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters could be arranged otherwise, once the a is taken out of them

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A chill audience response greets a piece played with a section cut.
explanation.walkthrough: C plus REACTION, with an A removed ('a bit's left out'), is rearranged ('perhaps') into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Plural of a work for soloist and orchestra, so pieces of music.

clue.text: Copper can interrupt

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a tin is a can

explanation.surface: A policeman is able to break into the conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a police officer but is the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: To butt into a conversation or dance is to break in.

clue.text: Spirit in bathing friend can bring small comfort

indicators.note: the drink goes inside the honour's letters

parts.note: CB is a Companion of the Bath, a British honour; companion means friend
rum is a spirit

explanation.surface: A drink while bathing with a pal is a little consolation.
explanation.walkthrough: CB is Companion of the (Order of the) Bath, a British order of knighthood; 'bathing friend' means that companion, not someone in the tub.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny scrap, as in the idiom a crumb of comfort.

clue.text: Join, or untie knot

indicators.note: to knot is to tangle, so the letters of untie get tangled

explanation.surface: Someone is told either to tie things together or to undo a knot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knot' rearranges UNTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To combine or bring together, a synonym.

clue.text: Stun and for some time, we hear

indicators.note: the word is judged by how it sounds when spoken, not how it is spelt

parts.note: days means a period of time, as in for days

explanation.surface: Someone is stunned and stays that way for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: To stupefy or bewilder someone, a synonym.

clue.text: Call to account at holding a rebellion

indicators.note: the word at holds the rebellion's letters inside it

parts.note: UDI, the Unilateral Declaration of Independence by Rhodesia in 1965, was a rebellion against the Crown

explanation.surface: Someone is held responsible for staging an uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: UDI is the 1965 Rhodesian break from Britain, a crossword stand-by for rebellion.
explanation.definitionFit: An official inspection of accounts calls someone to explain them.

clue.text: Colic? Kate's sick as a parrot!

indicators.note: feeling ill and out of sorts, so the letters of colic and Kate are disordered

parts.note: the possessive adds no letter

explanation.surface: Kate has a stomach ache and is very upset, as sick as a parrot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sick' rearranges COLIC KATE. 'Sick as a parrot' is British slang for bitterly disappointed.
explanation.definitionFit: A small crested Australian bird of the parrot family.

clue.text: Go astray and so by getting lost, can't deliver?

definitions.note: a whimsical description of messengers who have gone astray

parts.note: to err is to stray from the right path

indicators.note: going astray, so the letters of the three little words wander into a new order

explanation.surface: Messengers who stray and lose their way fail to make their drops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting lost' makes ANDBOYS. The question mark flags a jokey definition: lads who carry messages but, lost, cannot deliver them.
explanation.definitionFit: Young messengers whose job is carrying goods; lost ones fail at delivering.

clue.text: Sanctuary needed? Live with mother!

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
Ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: Someone needing refuge is told to move back home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sanctuary' looks like refuge; it means the raised platform in a synagogue or the chancel in an Orthodox church.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised platform or chancel area in a place of worship, the holy part of it.
